name: comp-481

frames.best_why: Email now sits ahead of Name after the drag, showing the completed reorder on full rows.

tagline: Table whose columns you can drag sideways into a new order.
summary: A dark five-column account table. Every header holds a small grip for dragging that column to a new place and an arrow button for sorting, and the rows move with the column mid-drag.
appearance: On black, a slightly lighter header band holds five labels, each preceded by a faint dotted grip and followed by a chevron. Rows show bold names, emails, a flag emoji with a city, plain status words, and right-aligned balances.
behaviour: Pressing a header's grip and sliding it sideways carries that column and its cells with it; Email is pulled in front of Name across the frames. Sorting arrows sit beside each label, and column order is kept only while the page stays open.
demo_content: Five employees with emails, country flags, status and balances; the caption credits two libraries.
search_phrases: table with columns you can drag around
reorder table columns by dragging headers
data table with grip handles in headers
move columns left or right in a table
custom column order table for admins
table headers with drag dots and arrows
use_when: People want to arrange a table's columns to their own taste and reorder them in place.
avoid_when: The chosen order lives only in memory, so a page reload snaps every column back to its starting place.
customise: Columns, labels and the fetch URL are written in the file; adding fields or saving the chosen column order needs a source edit.
weight_why: Two drag libraries plus remote rows, with only the moving column animating.

a11y.note: The drag grip has a label and keyboard sorting works, but the sort arrow buttons are icon-only with no accessible name.

issues: Sort buttons have no accessible name, only a hidden icon.
Column order resets on reload because nothing is persisted.
The caption credits two libraries instead of describing the example.
polish_why: Tidy dark table and a smooth column swap, but the header controls are tiny and unexplained.
title: Draggable Columns Table
